questions.prompt: A market buy of 400 shares meets a bar with open 101.5 and volume 1,700. With the 10% volume cap, what is the fill?
options: No fill, because the order is too large
questions.explanation: The cap is 1700 × 0.10 = 170 shares, so only 170 of the 400 trade. A market order fills at the bar's open of 101.5.

questions.prompt: A limit buy at 102.0 meets a bar with open 102.5, high 103.0 and low 98.5. At what price does it fill?
questions.explanation: The low of 98.5 reached the limit, so the order fills. Its price is the lower of the open (102.5) and the limit (102.0), which is 102.0.

questions.prompt: The signal reads the close of 2025-03-06. Why does the backtest fill the order at the open of 2025-03-07 instead of that close?
options: Because the open is always cheaper than the close
Because exchanges accept orders only at the open
Because a fill at the open is easier to code
Because the close is already in the past when the signal has its view, so the next open is the earliest price you can trade at
questions.explanation: The decision needs the close, so it is made after the close. The first price after that decision is the next bar's open, here 104.5 instead of 104.0.
